analysis:
Examined the ci.yml head text, the release-dev-branch.yml base, head and patch, and the release-provider.yml patch. The ci.yml and release-dev-branch.yml changes only add scripts/test-provider-cluster-runtime-models.py to the CI test list and two new scripts to the dev-push path filter. They change no permissions, secrets or triggers, so I found no regression there.

The main security-relevant change is in release-provider.yml (patch hunks near lines 66, 298, 941 and 1078). It adds a step that extracts the final signed bundle after its SHA-256 is checked against BUNDLE_HASH. The step deletes the signing keychain, asserts the identity is no longer listed, and runs scripts/provider-cluster-runtime-facts.sh, which the PR describes as running the app's CLI with an empty environment. The resulting cluster_runtime block is attached to release registration only when CLUSTER_RUNTIME_SEND is 'true'. That requires publish=='true' and the per-environment repository variable to equal 'true'. It is default-off, and without the variable a failure only warns. The keychain removal limits exposure of the signing identity to code that runs afterwards.

Open questions for deeper review; the supplied evidence does not show them to be flaws:
(1) The scripts provider-cluster-runtime-facts.sh, provider-cluster-runtime-models.py and the --cluster-runtime handling in provider-release-publication.py were not supplied. I could not verify the empty-environment execution, the extraction safety, or that the job's other env or secrets are not reachable by the app.
(2) The facts are computed by the built artifact itself and then feed coordinator-derived cluster approvals, pair-serving grants and parity qualifications. That is relevant to A-017 and T-054, which require independent qualification. Whether the coordinator treats them as non-authoritative inputs is platform-owned and unverified. The threat model may need a note that these facts are build-self-reported.
(3) The keychain is now deleted mid-job. Later steps must not need codesign, and any cleanup step must tolerate the missing keychain; I could not see the later steps.
(4) The dev lane still has no enforced review on `dev`, as documented in the pre-existing comments. This PR adds the facts computation to that lane.
(5) The retained artifact (30-day retention) holds cluster-runtime.json and release-models.json; their contents are not visible, so I could not assess disclosure.
